answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is a bonded identity with a costly challenge. Each new agent stakes a bond, then answers a fresh challenge seeded at random, a short sonnet that must carry the given words sparrow, sonnet and zenith. Peers check answers for coherence and duplication. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must post a thousand bonds and do the work for each one, so cost grows with every identity. Copied output gets flagged and its bond slashed. Honest agents keep their stake, while a sybil swarm burns money it cannot recover.
